title: Variables
description:
Variables are areas in memory that store data. That's all they are. However, it isn't that simple. Variables have many datatypes which determine what way the data stored inside of them is represented. In this lesson, we will cover the most common datatype: `int`. Int store any 32 bit _whole number_. That means any number between `-2147483648` and `2147483647`. Pretty big, right? To make a variable, you use the syntax `type name = value;`, or just `type name;`. If you initlize a variable with a value it will have that value, and if you don't, it will have the default value for that type. You can reassign variables just with `name = value`. 
 ## Assignment: 
 The TechQ Team wants a variable for lines of code in their code base! Make a variable `total_lines` with the value `26028`.
expectedOutput: TechQ Codebase is greater than 25k lines! Codebase size: 26028
hint: Remember to initlize the variable with the value 26028
